q-3131.name: Question 1
q-3131.problem: Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation $49{j}^{2}-64=0.$
q-3131.worked_solution:
Using the difference of squares formula, we factor the left-hand side of our quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}49{j}^{2}-64 & =0 \\ (7j)^{2}-{8}^{2} & =0 \\ (7j-8)(7j+8) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the zero product rule, we have

$$
7j-8=0\,\text{or}\,7j+8=0.
$$

Then, we solve each equation separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}7j-8 & =0 & \, & \, & 7j+8 & =0 \\ 7j & =8 & \, & \, & 7j & =-8 \\ j & =\frac{8}{7} & \, & \, & j & =-\frac{8}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $j=-\frac{8}{7},\frac{8}{7}.$ We can write this even more concisely as $j=\pm \frac{8}{7}.$

q-12785.name: Question 2
q-12785.problem: Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation $4{k}^{2}-36=0.$
q-12785.worked_solution:
Before we start our normal process of factoring, notice that all of the terms have a common factor of $4.$ Therefore, we can simplify the expression by factoring out $4,$ as follows:

$$
4{k}^{2}-36=4({k}^{2}-9)
$$

Now, let's factor the expression inside parentheses using the difference of squares formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}4({k}^{2}-9) & =0 \\ 4({k}^{2}-{3}^{2}) & =0 \\ 4(k-3)(k+3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the zero product rule, we have

$$
k-3=0\,\text{or}\,k+3=0,
$$

which in turn gives

$$
k=3\,\text{or}\,k=-3.
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $k=-3,3.$ We can write this even more concisely as $k=\pm 3.$

q-23553.name: Question 3
q-23553.problem: Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation $4{x}^{2}=25.$
q-23553.worked_solution:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and collect the like terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2} & =25 \\ 4{x}^{2}-25 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the difference of squares formula, we factor the left-hand side of our quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-25 & =0 \\ (2x)^{2}-(5)^{2} & =0 \\ (2x-5)(2x+5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the zero product rule, we have

$$
2x-5=0\,\text{or}\,2x+5=0.
$$

Then, we solve each equation separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-5 & =0 & \, & \, & 2x+5 & =0 \\ 2x & =5 & \, & \, & 2x & =-5 \\ x & =\frac{5}{2} & \, & \, & x & =-\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=-\frac{5}{2},\frac{5}{2}.$ We can write this even more concisely as $x=\pm \frac{5}{2}.$
